data.rows_per_pair_enforced_by: src/training/lora.py sample_pairs() raises unless every chosen pair has exactly 8 rows
pool_pairs_rationale: exactly enough: pool_rows equals the largest k, so no unused remainder
identical to report 15 exp002 (sample_pairs(n_pairs=250, seed=0) on the same file), so the permutation is the same one and exp002's 200 rows are the first 200 of this order
far below the 1198-pair ceiling of the split

measurement_intervals.interval_clock: time.monotonic() inside each process; monotonic clocks are NEVER compared across processes, and wall clock is recorded for alignment only, never computed with
measurement_intervals.withdrawn_design: An earlier version required a foreground safety probe every row AND a 30s maximum gap AND no background thread. Those three cannot hold together: a foreground probe can only run between rows, so a 95 s/row row (the old control's measured worst window) makes a 30s ceiling unreachable, and 'a gap over 30s counts as a probe failure' would misfire on legitimately slow rows.
measurement_intervals.adopted_design: Split recording from enforcement. Recording: the child probes in the foreground every 5 rows into memory[]. Enforcement: a separate watchdog process, started by the parent before the child is spawned, polls OS-level numbers every 5.0s and can ask the child to stop. The prohibition on a background thread INSIDE the measured process is unchanged, and its reason -- not perturbing the thing being measured -- is preserved.

gate_wait.note: happens in the parent, before the child exists; not a segment of the child's timeline

condition_clock.starts: the instant row 1 begins, after model load

clocks.model_load_seconds: inside process_clock, outside condition_clock; teardown likewise
clocks.removed_field: non_overlapping: true was wrong -- condition_clock is a sub-interval of process_clock, not a disjoint sibling

primary_metric.name: D100
primary_metric.definition: mean(seconds_per_row over final 100 rows) / mean(seconds_per_row over first 100 rows)
primary_metric.basis: model_compute_seconds per row, from the stored per_row array
primary_metric.note: D100 is the single primary metric, but the Q1 verdict is NOT D100 alone -- see verdicts.Q1_run

secondary_metrics.D20: last 20-row window / first 20-row window (same shape as reports 14 and 15)
secondary_metrics.Dmax: max over all 20-row windows / mean(first 100 rows)

safety_policy.priority: protect the machine first; letting any arm finish is NOT a goal
safety_policy.acknowledged_asymmetry: identical thresholds can still produce condition-correlated stops, because the continuous arm is the one that drives memory (at 200 rows: driver 54.4 GB, swap 8.36 GB, pressure 7 %free). This is a property of the condition, not a bias in the rule, and cannot be removed by tuning thresholds. A stopped run is simply not a complete arm.
safety_policy.withdrawn_rationale: the earlier justification 'chosen so they do not selectively terminate the control arm' put measurement convenience ahead of machine safety and is withdrawn

thresholds.swap_used_gb_max_basis: one quarter of 48 GB physical; the 200-row control already reached 8.36 GB, so a 2000-row control is EXPECTED to trip this
thresholds.swap_growth_basis: 2 GB of swap growth within a single row is runaway
thresholds.memory_pressure_basis: the 200-row control reached 7 %free; 5 %free is the macOS red zone; 5 consecutive probes avoids transient dips
thresholds.free_plus_inactive_basis: SECONDARY signal only. The 200-row control reached 0.405 GB with no harm, so a floor above that would refuse a state the machine is known to tolerate. inactive pages are reclaimable: this is neither free nor available memory.
thresholds.slow_row_basis: a hang detector, NOT a performance threshold; the old 2000-row control's worst window of 95.0 s/row is normal degradation, above 120 looks like a stall
thresholds.max_seconds_basis: condition_clock bound; old control 5.76h, ~1.4x headroom, still bounded
thresholds.process_max_seconds_basis: 30 minutes above max_seconds, so a stall during model load or teardown is also bounded

safety_policy.consecutive_unit: 'consecutive probes' means consecutive WATCHDOG polls (~25s for 5 polls), not rows. swap_growth_gb_per_probe_max is likewise measured between adjacent watchdog polls.

stop_sequence.1_stop_request: the watchdog writes stop_request.json (rule, values, monotonic, wall clock, nonce) plus stop_request.sha256, THEN sends SIGTERM to the child's PROCESS GROUP
stop_sequence.2_signal_handler: the child's SIGTERM handler ONLY sets a flag. No JSON, no file I/O, nothing that is not async-signal-safe.
stop_sequence.3_next_safe_row_boundary: the child checks the flag at the next safe row boundary, reads stop_request.json and verifies its SHA-256 and nonce; a digest or nonce mismatch is REJECTED and recorded as stop_request_rejected (a tool failure)
stop_sequence.4_partial_report: on a verified request the child writes its partial report with stopped_early = {condition, rule, row, sampled_values, condition_clock_seconds, process_clock_seconds, requested_by: 'watchdog', stop_request_sha256} and exits 0, so partial results survive
stop_sequence.5_grace_clock: measured on the WATCHDOG's own time.monotonic() -- not the parent's, not wall clock
stop_sequence.6_sigkill: on grace expiry, re-check child_start_identity and then SIGKILL the process group; the child writes no report => outcome no_report => TERMINAL INCOMPLETE, NOT an R1 cancellation

parent_supervision.rule: the parent watches child, watchdog and heartbeat CONCURRENTLY while the child runs; it must NOT wait for the child to exit before noticing the watchdog died

watches.how: Popen.poll() -- the watchdog is also the parent's child process
watches.on_bad: IMMEDIATELY request the child to stop

watches.how: the watchdog sends a heartbeat over IPC after each poll; the parent records the last one on its own monotonic clock
watches.on_bad: gap > 30.0s => IMMEDIATELY request the child to stop

parent_supervision.withdrawn: the earlier post-hoc watchdog_gap check (comparing timestamps only after the child exited) is withdrawn and replaced by this live supervision

steps: 2. per-file source verification passes           (no boot consumed)
3. start the watchdog, wait for its ready handshake  (no boot consumed, child not yet bound)
4. atomically write measurement_started          (*** the boot is consumed here ***)
5. spawn the child in a NEW process group
6. hand the child's identity to the watchdog over the pipe/socketpair
7. watchdog replies armed and begins enforcing
8. the parent enters the three-way supervision loop

failure_semantics.result: gate_attempt or pre_spawn_abort; NO boot consumed; retryable in the same boot

failure_semantics.at: 3 (watchdog fails to start, or ready times out)
failure_semantics.result: measurement_started MUST NOT be written and NO boot is consumed; write a retryable watchdog_launch_failed event; retryable in the same boot after a fix
measurement_started was already written at 4, so the boot is spent => TERMINAL INCOMPLETE with outcome no_report

failure_semantics.at: 8 (watchdog dies or heartbeat gap during the run)
failure_semantics.result: request the child to stop; TOOL FAILURE => TERMINAL INCOMPLETE

child_identity.why: the watchdog must never target a bare PID: a PID can be reused and the wrong process killed

fields.child_pgid: process group; SIGTERM/SIGKILL are sent to the PROCESS GROUP, never to a bare PID
fields.nonce: secrets.token_hex(16), generated per launch, NEVER reused; written to launch.json and passed to the child, which echoes it in its report
fields.child_start_identity: the child's process start time, so 'same PID' and 'same process' can be told apart

child_identity.pid_reuse_guard: re-check child_start_identity immediately before signalling; on mismatch send NOTHING, record identity_mismatch and have the parent finalise

measurement_results_only: a real safety threshold trip (swap / pressure / free+inactive / slow_row / max_seconds / process_max_seconds)
tool_failure_rules: MUST NOT be written as Q1 = fails
if it happens AFTER measurement_started: the boot is spent => TERMINAL INCOMPLETE, and only a NEW experiment id may run again
if it happens BEFORE measurement_started (step 3): no boot consumed, retryable in the same boot
tool_failure_vs_measurement.why: writing 'our supervisor crashed' as 'the treatment failed to hold' turns a tool bug into an experimental conclusion -- exactly what this project has been guarding against

watchdog_poll_failure_rules.single_failure: record null values plus the failure reason string
watchdog_poll_failure_rules.streak_effect: a failed poll NEITHER advances NOR resets any violation streak
watchdog_poll_failure_rules.on_streak_exceeded: request the child to stop with reason probe_unavailable -- which is a TOOL FAILURE, see tool_failure_vs_measurement
watchdog_poll_failure_rules.late_poll_counts_as_failure: a time.monotonic() gap over 30.0s between adjacent watchdog polls counts as one failure; the watchdog does not wait for row boundaries, so a slow row cannot misfire it

on_real_safety_trip: the run is NOT a complete arm and may not feed the headline
do NOT relax any threshold and re-run
Q1_run = fails, taking PRIORITY over the metrics, and holding even when D100/Dmax are null for lack of rows
Q2_run keeps its real value when computable, but is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY and can never support adoption
per the decision matrix, neither a safety trip nor any tool failure may lead straight to option C

clear_cost_checks.expected_positions: [10, 20, ..., k] where k is that run's declared row count; checked row by row, not only counted
clear_cost_checks.growth_valid_at_k500: k=500 gives 50 calls, so the first 20 and last 20 do not overlap

same_array_identity.applies_to: values derived from the same unrounded array, e.g. per-call sum vs recorded total

different_summation_order.applies_to: seconds derived by different accumulation orders, e.g. row-span sum vs per-call sum

float_tolerances.display_rounded_values: display only; must never take part in an identity check

loss_engineering_tolerance.applies_to: prefix consistency between runs of different declared lengths
loss_engineering_tolerance.basis: pre-selected engineering tolerance, same as report 15; NOT derived from report 14's four-decimal storage

float_tolerances.integer_fields: exact equality, no tolerance (clear_calls, tokens, row numbers)

verdicts.note: Three-state with a declared indeterminate band. 'indeterminate' is an allowed outcome and must be reported as such.

Q1_run.real_safety_trip_takes_priority: swap / pressure / free+inactive / slow_row / max_seconds / process_max_seconds -- any of these makes Q1_run = 'fails' REGARDLESS of whether D100/Dmax are computable; the metrics are then null + reason
Q1_run.fails: any REAL safety threshold tripped (PRIORITY); or D100 >= 3.0; or Dmax >= 6.0
Q1_run.holds: no safety threshold tripped AND D100 <= 1.5 AND Dmax <= 3.0 (both computable)
Q1_run.indeterminate: no safety threshold tripped, metrics computable, values in the middle band
Q1_run.not_applicable: no safety threshold tripped, but D100 or Dmax could not be computed for lack of rows

Q2_run.not_driven_by_safety_trips: a safety trip speaks to Q1, not Q2; it does not make Q2 'scales'
Q2_run.on_safety_trip: if enough rows remain, KEEP the real Q2_run value (it was genuinely computed) but mark it descriptive only -- it can never support adoption, which requires Q1_plan == holds_to_2000. Only insufficient rows give not_applicable.
Q2_run.indeterminate: both computable, values in the middle band
Q2_run.not_applicable: clear_growth is null (fewer than 400 rows); clear_share is still reported but is DESCRIPTIVE only

repeatability.metric: P(a..b) = mean compute seconds per row over rows a..b for one run; R(a..b) = max over runs / min over runs
repeatability.basis: exp002's two treatment runs (different boots, different block positions) had full-run means of 1.3107 and 1.3087, R = 1.0015; 1.10 is a loose engineering band that still catches a real boot-to-boot difference
repeatability.window_dispersion: max relative deviation of the 100-row aggregates within the same span -- descriptive only, not a criterion

applies_to.A: not claimed -- a single run leaves R undefined

verdicts.thresholds_are_not_pass_marks_derived_fr: The 200-row readings (treatment D20 = 0.77 / 0.87, clear share ~2%) motivated these numbers but are not the criterion. The criterion is this table, frozen before any run.

Q1_plan.holds_to_1000: k=1000 is 'holds' but k=2000 did not reach 'holds' and is not 'fails'
Q1_plan.holds_to_500: k=500 is 'holds' but k=1000 did not reach 'holds' and is not 'fails'
Q1_plan.fails: some run's Q1_run is 'fails'; k_fail records the first
Q1_plan.indeterminate: no run 'fails', but the longest completed run is 'indeterminate'
Q1_plan.not_applicable: no run produced a computable Q1 verdict
Q1_plan.k_star: largest k whose Q1_run is 'holds', else null
Q1_plan.k_fail: first k whose Q1_run is 'fails', else null

Q2_plan.aggregates_only: runs that actually completed AND whose Q2_run is computable, i.e. Q2_run in {stable, scales, indeterminate}
Q2_plan.excluded: runs whose Q2_run is not_applicable do not take part and do not drag the aggregate to indeterminate
Q2_plan.stable: all contributing runs are 'stable' and at least one contributes

tool_failure_produces_no_verdict.rule: if a run ended in a TOOL FAILURE, Q1_run = null with Q1_reason = 'tool_failure: <which>' and Q2_run = null with the same reason
tool_failure_produces_no_verdict.why: not_applicable means 'this measurement cannot decide'; a tool failure means 'this was not a measurement at all'. The two must never impersonate each other.
tool_failure_produces_no_verdict.consequence: terminal incomplete, and R1 does not fire

conditional_stop_rule.statement: After the measurement_finished event of a run whose outcome is 'completed' AND which had NO tool failure, the parent RECOMPUTES that run's Q1_run verdict from the child's per_row array and watchdog.jsonl (never trusting any conclusion field the child wrote). If the verdict is 'fails', every not-yet-executed run in the plan is cancelled by rule. 'holds', 'indeterminate' and 'not_applicable' all continue.
conditional_stop_rule.indeterminate_continues_because: a longer run is exactly what turns indeterminate or not_applicable into a definite verdict
conditional_stop_rule.b1_decision_input: the complete Q1_run verdict (stop conditions FIRST, then D100 and Dmax, both of which must be computable for 'holds'), not D100 alone. At k=500 both D100 and Dmax are computable (500 >= 200, >= 120) and clear_growth is too (50 calls >= 40). The decision is made by the rule, not by the operator at the time.
replay_checks: the triggering run's outcome is actually 'completed' AND it had no tool failure
recompute the Q1_run verdict from the triggering child's per_row and watchdog.jsonl and compare field by field; uncomputable fields must be null + reason, and a 0 is treated as tampering
the recomputed verdict must actually be 'fails', and its cause must be a real safety threshold or a computable D100/Dmax
cancelled_runs must equal exactly the plan's not-yet-executed runs at that point
no cancelled run may have a measurement_started event
conditional_stop_rule.why_this_is_legal_in_an_immutable_plan: the plan declares all three runs AND rule R1 from the start, and the rule text is inside plan_digest; cancelling is not editing the plan, it is following a branch the plan already declared, and anyone can recompute from disk that the branch was taken correctly
conditional_stop_rule.not_r1: every entry of never_fires_on goes to terminal_rules; they are TOOL FAILURES with no Q1 verdict for R1 to act on

replay_rules: read-only; recompute everything, never read back a conclusion
recompute thresholds from calibration samples and compare the digest
replay every gate poll and recompute streak, passed, waited, timeout
recompute all windows and D100/D20/Dmax from per_row; when rows are insufficient the value must be null -- a 0 is treated as tampering
check clear positions row by row against [10, ..., k]; per-call sum == recorded total == row-span sum, under the float tolerances
check the clock nesting invariant: model_load_seconds + condition_clock_seconds <= process_clock_seconds; gate wait does not appear in it (different process)

recompute every safety rule and its consecutive counters from watchdog.jsonl (whose digest must match the finished event), using its own monotonic field for poll intervals; confirm that what should have stopped did, that what did not stop should not have, and that the SIGTERM/SIGKILL timing matches the grace period. Never trust the child's stopped_early; the child's every-5-rows memory[] is corroboration, not the enforcement record
prefix consistency on sample_id, tokens, supervised_tokens and loss -- and with a single run it must be not_applicable, never passed
replay the journal: consecutive events, experiment_id, started/finished digest backlink, one measurement_started per run, distinct boots
recompute the plan-level state machine: any plan_arm_cancelled event fired exactly when it should have, and the run that triggered it had outcome 'completed'
fail closed on any missing recovery field

cross_report_prefix_check.claim: because pool_pairs=250, seed=0 and the same instruct_inv_train.jsonl, report 16's order is the SAME permutation as report 15 exp002's, so exp002's 200 rows are rows 1..200 of report 16's order
cross_report_prefix_check.why_not: it only holds if the new script consumes RNG in exactly the same order as scripts/15_mps_order.py; dropout 0.05 is stochastic and any extra tensor creation shifts the RNG stream
cross_report_prefix_check.on_mismatch: record it and explain the difference; it does NOT affect Q1 or Q2 (those are timing questions inside one script), but report 16's per-row values may not then be quoted against exp002's

That claim was wrong and is withdrawn. exp002's durability rests on exp002/source_snapshot/ plus the digests in session.json and the child records; replay_session_journal() reads a finished session with check_working_tree=False, and verify_sources() checks only the snapshot in that mode. Editing a shared module later would change only an informational live-tree comparison column if the Markdown were re-rendered -- it would not invalidate the run or fail --verify.

a new file has a much smaller regression surface

record the change and the re-verification in PROJECT_STATUS.md

immutable_plan_procedure.1: freeze this design file and record its sha256
immutable_plan_procedure.2: --session-init reads this JSON and embeds the constants verbatim into plan.json, recording this file's sha256 inside the plan for traceability
immutable_plan_procedure.3: plan_digest = sha256(canonical_json(plan)); published with os.link atomic no-clobber, EEXIST if the destination exists

'clearing has been proven effective at long range' -- B shows the treatment did not degrade badly, not its gain over not clearing
any arithmetic that uses the old 2000-row record (13.1x) as a paired comparator

not_enough: Q2_plan == 'not_applicable' (an uncomputed cost is not a bounded cost)
engineering_adoption_requires.why: Q1 alone with a scaling cost means degradation is controlled but the cost eats the benefit at length; Q2 alone with Q1 failing is worse
engineering_adoption_requires.strongest_permitted_statement: on this machine, this configuration and within 2000 rows, this mitigation is stable in itself and its cost is bounded -- still NOT 'proven better than not clearing'

limits: a fresh process resets this process's allocator, heap, model and optimizer; it does not prove the OS or driver returned to a comparable state
the gate certifies the start of a run only; a 45-minute or 6-hour run is never re-gated, and should not be
a long run spans thermal states and macOS background activity; the design records this and cannot control it
all durations use a monotonic clock; wall clock is recorded but never computed with
long runs are expensive to repeat, so n stays small: B is n=1 at the full 2000 rows and n=3 on the 500-row prefix -- engineering signal, not a variance estimate
the old 2000-row record has eight provenance gaps and is a scheduling/risk prior only

the safety thresholds are conservative values set from 200-row observations and machine specs, not derived from long-run data; they may stop a run that was in fact safe, and may be insufficient for some unanticipated failure mode. What is guaranteed is only: frozen in advance, identical across conditions, fully recorded on trip, and never relaxed for a re-run

the watchdog is another process: it can itself be delayed by the scheduler, slowed by memory pressure, or killed. The late-poll and failure rules and the watchdog_gap check DETECT that, they do not PREVENT it. Under extreme paging, 'the protection slows down too' is a real failure mode this design does not claim to exclude
no option answers mechanism, other machines, other OS/torch versions, other model sizes, other row-length distributions, or lengths beyond 2000

partial_run_metric_semantics.rule: If a metric cannot be computed, write null and a *_reason string of the form 'not_applicable: <why>'. NEVER write 0 -- 0 is a measured value, and writing it makes 'could not be computed' look like 'computed as zero', which is exactly the mistake exp001's stored within_tolerance=false made.
partial_run_metric_semantics.D100_note: needs 200 rows so the first and last 100 do not overlap
partial_run_metric_semantics.Dmax_note: needs the first 100 rows plus at least one complete 20-row window
partial_run_metric_semantics.clear_share_on_partial_runs: computable from any run with at least one row, but on a partial run it is DESCRIPTIVE only and may not decide Q2 on its own
partial_run_metric_semantics.examples_must_not_contain_zero: every worked example in the design writes null + a *_reason string; a 0 in a metric field is treated as tampering by replay

no safety threshold tripped AND no tool failure of any kind (probe_unavailable, watchdog death, heartbeat gap, identity_mismatch, stop_request_rejected)
the three runs came from three distinct boots
all cross-run provenance fields identical (only k may differ)
all three runs honoured the treatment contract

terminal_rules.rule: once a measured run has started and not successfully finished, the whole experiment is TERMINAL INCOMPLETE: neither that boot nor any later boot may re-run it; only a NEW experiment id with the full plan may follow
terminal_rules.parent_crash: a started event with no finished event is terminal incomplete too, recorded by --session-finalize
terminal_rules.finalize: --session-finalize writes an incomplete aggregate and report WITHOUT re-running anything

boundary_with_R1.case: run completed with no tool failure, recomputed Q1 = fails
watchdog SIGTERM on a REAL safety trip, child wrote a partial report and exited 0
boundary_with_R1.state: outcome completed + stopped_early => Q1 fails => complete_by_rule

boundary_with_R1.case: watchdog SIGKILL after the 120s grace, no report
watchdog failed to launch, BEFORE measurement_started

terminal_rules.must_not_conflate: a terminal incomplete is NOT an R1 cancellation, may NOT produce an early_stop_finding, and may NOT be described as 'closed early by rule' -- that would dress a failed execution up as a conclusion
terminal_rules.tool_failure_after_started: always terminal incomplete; the same experiment may NOT re-run that run just because 'it was only the tool' -- the boot is spent and the machine state has moved on. A NEW experiment id is required.

watchdog_log_durability.create: the FINAL path is created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL -- no temp-then-rename, no overwrite; FileExistsError if it already exists
watchdog_log_durability.seq: starts at 0 and increases by exactly 1
watchdog_log_durability.prev_digest: sha256 of the PREVIOUS record's exact line bytes; null for seq 0; forms a hash chain
watchdog_log_durability.flush_and_fsync: every record is flush()ed AND os.fsync()ed immediately, so neither a power loss nor SIGKILL can leave a half-written last line
watchdog_log_durability.seal: once the finished event is produced the file is sealed: no further appends, and the WHOLE-FILE sha256 goes into the finished event alongside the report digest
replay_must_reject: a truncated line (the last line is not complete JSON) -- parsing failure is a rejection, never 'skip the last line'
missing seq (seq must be the complete range 0..n-1)
out-of-order seq (file order must equal increasing seq order)
an inserted record (the next record's prev_digest no longer matches)
a deleted record (same, plus a seq gap)
a rewritten record (its digest changed, so the next prev_digest fails)
an append after the finished event (whole-file sha256 no longer matches the finished event)
watchdog_log_durability.monotonic_scope: the monotonic field is used for poll intervals WITHIN this log only; it is never compared with the child's or the parent's monotonic clock

hardening_third_round.journal: schema_version, kind, contiguous index, experiment_id, plan_digest, run_id, written_at and previous_event_digest on every event; finished records started_index and the started file's sha256; validator checks plan order, the closed event set, at most one started and one finished per run, and body run/event/experiment/plan identity
hardening_third_round.locking: session_next takes a NON-BLOCKING exclusive lock BEFORE reading the journal, then re-reads the journal, next run, boot and terminal state inside it; finalize and R1 take the same lock
hardening_third_round.completed_outcome: qualify_outcome() requires a non-bool integer 0 exit AND a report AND a watchdog log that both exist and match their recorded digests; a bare {'outcome': 'completed'} is downgraded to no_report
hardening_third_round.calibration: validated at session-init (samples, thresholds, fixed policy, thresholds recompute) and again by verify; the gate uses the thresholds recomputed from the calibration and the fixed policy, and verify replays every poll recomputing streak, passed, waited and the timeout
hardening_third_round.watchdog_process_ceiling: enforced from the watchdog's OWN monotonic elapsed time, checked before any early return, so a child wedged before it ever writes progress is still stopped at 30,600s
hardening_third_round.progress_rules: progress that never arrives is normal while a model loads and is bounded by the process ceiling; progress that arrives and stops advancing is progress_stalled, an explicit tool failure
hardening_third_round.nonce: cross-checked against the parent's independent launch record, never against the identity being checked
hardening_third_round.replay: loads and authenticates the stop request by digest and nonce, replays action order, heartbeat sequence, the SIGTERM reason and the 120s grace
hardening_third_round.r1: runs automatically inside session_next after a qualifying finished run, records the report and watchdog digests it recomputed from, and its recorded verdict is compared field by field on replay
hardening_third_round.aggregate: every derived field is compared against a fresh derivation, not a shortlist; missing and unknown fields are both rejected

fourth_round.production_child: run_child() is no longer a placeholder: it builds the frozen 250-pair / 2000-row pool, takes the seed=0 permutation over row indices, truncates to the run's k, loads tokenizer, model, LoRA and AdamW, times every row, clears on every 10th, records analysis data and a progress line on every 5th, authenticates any stop request at a row boundary, and writes a full report atomically with no-clobber. Dependencies are injected through ChildDeps; tests drive THAT function with FakeChildDeps rather than a substitute child.
fourth_round.progress_stall_accounting: a row that advances resets progress_stall_polls to zero; only a repeated row accumulates; a row that goes backwards, is not an int, is a bool, or is below 1 is refused as progress_invalid
fourth_round.preconditions_before_the_gate: session_next replays calibration digest, samples to thresholds, the fixed policy, the session thresholds, plan and session identity, the source snapshot, the journal and every finished run's child and watchdog evidence -- inside the lock and BEFORE the gate. Any problem means the gate is never polled, no event is written and no boot is spent.
fourth_round.one_provenance_list: PROVENANCE_FIELDS is the single section 4.6 list, used by the child writer, single-run replay and the cross-run comparison. A field missing from every run now fails: identical absence is not agreement.
fourth_round.design_digest_is_informational: a changed design file on disk is reported in notes, not problems, matching what the design says. The plan embeds frozen_constants verbatim under plan_digest, so the file on disk cannot change what a run was judged by.

frozen_constants.note: THE machine-readable authority. --session-init reads this block and embeds it verbatim into plan.json; src/training/longrun.py cross-checks its own module constants against it and refuses to build a plan on any mismatch, so there can never be a second set of constants quietly winning.

zero_semantics.rule: zero is a legitimate measurement. A ratio whose tail genuinely measured 0.0 is stored as 0.0 and passes replay.
zero_semantics.null_is_only_for: a value that cannot be computed at all -- too few rows, or a zero baseline that makes the ratio undefined -- and it always carries a *_reason
zero_semantics.replay: stored and recomputed are compared in BOTH directions: a computable metric stored as null is rejected, an uncomputable metric stored with a value is rejected, a mismatched reason is rejected, and unexpected or missing keys are rejected
